newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says Spanish operators order FCT.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says Spanish operators order FCT.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Tuesday that Spanish operators had placed orders for several thousand fixed cellular terminal (FCT) systems and had options for several thousand more in 1997.
Initial deliveries took place during the second quarter, the company said in a statement without disclosing the value of the order.

"In the first significant implementation of Ericsson's innovative FCT system, Spanish operators have begun providing small-business subscribers with fixed telephony services over radio, using Ericsson's GSM based FCT system," it said.

The system supports conventional telephones, fax machines or computers in homes or offices using a wireless network instead of conventional telephone wires. The system is also known as fixed wireless.
"You can deliver service to a greater number of subscribers in less time," Claes Wiberg, product manager for fixed cellular at the business unit Ericsson Radio Systems in Stockholm, said.
